article.headline: Memory and Semis Pull More Call Volume Than the S&P 500
article.lede: The options market has a way of concentrating the mind. When Micron Technology (MU), Intel (INTC), and the newly independent SanDisk (SNDK) each attract more call option volume than SPY — the SPDR S&P 500 ETF and the world's most liquid derivatives instrument — the speculation is not hedging the broad market but making a high-conviction directional bet on a specific sector. @themarketear's observation, posted against a chart of the Nasdaq 100 at new all-time highs near 28,500 in May 2026 after surviving a sharp 2025 tariff-driven correction, captures a market mind entirely focused on the AI infrastructure stack.
article.body:
The three names represent the full memory and compute hierarchy being rebuilt for artificial intelligence. Micron Technology (MU) is the *DRAM* and *HBM* play: its second-quarter FY2026 revenue hit $23.86 billion, up 196% year-on-year, with its entire HBM supply sold out through all of calendar 2026. HBM, or *High-Bandwidth Memory*, is DRAM stacked three-dimensionally to deliver the extreme bandwidth that GPU-based AI training demands; Micron's HBM4 product began volume shipments in early 2026 aligned with NVIDIA's (NVDA) Vera Rubin GPU platform, and the company projects the HBM total addressable market growing from roughly $35 billion in 2025 to $100 billion by 2028.

SanDisk (SNDK) represents the storage layer. The pure-play *NAND flash* company was spun out of Western Digital (WDC) in February 2025 and has traded as an independent Nasdaq-listed entity since February 24 of that year. It reported fourth-quarter FY2026 revenue guidance of $8 billion — roughly 23% above consensus — with its data-centre business up 645% year-on-year in the prior quarter. NAND flash prices are forecast to surge 234% in 2026, per Gartner (IT), a supply squeeze driven by the same AI data-centre buildout that has absorbed most production capacity. The stock has gained roughly 3,400% since its listing, and some circulating analyst price targets of $4,000 per share warrant appropriate scepticism.

Intel (INTC) is the more complex case. Long written off as a cycle casualty, the company has mounted a credible comeback under CEO Lip-Bu Tan, appointed in March 2025 after the board removed Pat Gelsinger following a stretch of punishing revenue declines. First-quarter 2026 revenue of $13.6 billion beat consensus by roughly 10%, with the Data Centre and AI segment rising 22% year-on-year. The proximate catalyst for fresh call buying arrived on May 5, when a report that Apple (AAPL) is in talks to manufacture chips on Intel's 18A *process node* — its most advanced *foundry* technology — sent the stock up 13% in a single session. Tan has argued that "the CPU is reinserting itself as the indispensable foundation of the AI era," pointing to *agentic AI* workloads — autonomous systems that act across multi-step tasks — as a new driver of general-purpose compute demand beyond GPUs.

The chart @themarketear posted shows the full Nasdaq 100 (*NDX*) arc that frames this moment: a February 2025 all-time high near 22,000, a sharp tariff-driven correction that took the index down roughly 23% peak-to-trough following the April 2025 "Liberation Day" tariff announcements, and a subsequent recovery that has carried the NDX to roughly 28,500 by May 2026, erasing the drawdown and setting new records. The call volume signal arrives not from a market in fear but from one that has survived a genuine shock and is rotating into high-conviction sector plays rather than broad passive exposure. When traders buy SPY calls, they are hedging or following the tape. When they buy calls on specific memory names with more urgency than they buy SPY calls, they are making a directional statement about which companies sit at the bottleneck of the next investment cycle.

The signal carries deliberate ambiguity. On one reading it validates the AI memory *supercycle* thesis: smart money positioning into names with sold-out capacity, exploding revenues, and structural pricing tailwinds. SK hynix (000660.KS), Micron's chief HBM rival, has characterised 2026 as "a supercycle similar to the boom of the 1990s"; Bank of America forecasts DRAM revenue up 51% in 2026, NAND revenue up 45%. On the other reading, concentrated call volume in narrow names is a classic late-cycle froth indicator — exactly the sentiment extreme that, when it unwinds, produces sharp corrections. The Roundhill Memory ETF, trading under the ticker DRAM, saw call volume 317% above its daily average on May 4 alone, suggesting the enthusiasm is sector-wide rather than limited to a handful of accounts. @themarketear leaves the interpretation open — "tells you exactly where this market's mind is right now" contains no explicit verdict — and that restraint is the sharpest part of the observation.

concepts.definition: A call option gives its buyer the right to purchase a stock at a fixed price before a set date. When call volume — the number of call contracts traded — spikes sharply in a name, it typically signals traders making leveraged directional bets that the stock will rise. Comparing individual-stock call volume to SPY, the world's most actively traded derivatives instrument, reveals where speculative conviction is concentrated.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, which tracks the S&P 500 index and has the largest and most liquid options market of any single instrument in the world. It is used by institutions to hedge broad equity exposure and by speculators to trade macro direction. When a single company's call volume rivals or exceeds SPY's, it registers an extraordinary concentration of directional bets in that name.

Dynamic Random-Access Memory — the dominant form of volatile computer memory used in servers, laptops, and phones. In AI data centres, DRAM sits between the processor and storage, and demand for high-speed, high-capacity configurations has surged with the expansion of large language model training and inference at scale.

High-Bandwidth Memory is DRAM stacked vertically in multiple layers and connected through tiny through-silicon vias, delivering far more data bandwidth than conventional flat DRAM. Modern AI accelerators depend on HBM because training large neural networks requires moving vast quantities of data in and out of memory at speeds that conventional DRAM cannot match. Supply is effectively controlled by three companies: SK hynix, Micron, and Samsung.

A type of non-volatile storage memory — it retains data without power, unlike DRAM. NAND is the technology inside solid-state drives, USB sticks, and data-centre storage arrays. In the AI era, enterprise NAND has become a bottleneck as cloud providers fill facilities with storage for model weights, training datasets, and inference caches.

A shorthand for the manufacturing technology generation used to fabricate a chip, historically named after a physical feature size in nanometres (Intel's 18A refers to 1.8 angstroms, a unit of length). Smaller nodes allow more transistors per area, lower power, and higher performance. The naming has become partly a marketing convention, but the underlying capability differences between generations remain real.

A semiconductor fabrication facility that manufactures chips designed by other companies — a "fab for hire." Intel historically designed and manufactured its own chips; its push to become an external foundry through Intel Foundry Services puts it in competition with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Samsung for customers willing to pay to have their chip designs built on Intel's process technology.

AI systems designed to act autonomously across multi-step tasks — browsing, coding, scheduling, making decisions — rather than simply answering single queries. Because agentic workloads run longer chains of inference and require more compute per session than simple chatbot interactions, they are expected to drive sustained demand for both specialised AI accelerators and general-purpose processors.

A sustained, multi-year period of above-trend pricing and demand in the DRAM or NAND flash industry, distinct from the shorter inventory-driven boom-bust cycles that have historically defined the sector. Analysts apply the term when structural supply shortfalls — here, driven by AI infrastructure demand — appear likely to persist for several years rather than self-correcting in the normal 12–18 month window.

The Nasdaq 100 index, which tracks the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. Heavily weighted toward US technology and semiconductor companies, it serves as the primary market barometer for the technology sector's health and is the underlying index for the QQQ ETF and a large suite of futures and options contracts.

The name the Trump White House gave to its April 2, 2025 announcement of sweeping new import tariffs on goods from dozens of countries. The announcement triggered one of the sharpest two-day declines in the Nasdaq 100 since 2007, followed a week later by a partial 90-day pause that sparked an equally violent relief rally. The episode produced the dominant macro narrative for equity markets through much of 2025.

article.fact_check: One auto-fetched background source (ibafin.com) incorrectly identifies MU as "Microchip Technology" and credits it with acquiring Microsemi Corporation — a transaction that belongs to Microchip Technology (MCHP), a separate company. MU is Micron Technology, a DRAM and NAND flash manufacturer. The ibafin source appears to have been generated by a low-quality AI summariser and should be disregarded entirely. The core claim in the tweet — that MU, INTC, and SNDK traded more call volume than SPY on the day of the post — is directionally consistent with documented unusual options activity across semiconductor names in the same period (including a 317% above-average call-volume day in the Roundhill Memory ETF on May 4), though precise per-name, per-day comparison figures against SPY were not independently verified from a primary exchange source.

ticker_mu.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
ticker_mu.blurb: Micron is the only US-headquartered manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory at scale, competing with Samsung and SK Hynix. Historically the most cyclical of the three, it has spent the past two years repositioning toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked DRAM that pairs with AI accelerators, where pricing is multiples of standard DDR5 and contracts are multi-year rather than spot.
ticker_mu.recent: In March 2026 Micron began mass production of HBM4 12-Hi 36GB stacks for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform; management has stated 2026 HBM capacity is sold out under binding agreements. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue was around $23.9 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin near 75%. The board approved a 30% dividend increase and roughly $25 billion of fiscal-2026 capex. Despite a strong year-to-date move, the forward P/E remains in the high single digits on consensus, reflecting residual cyclicality scepticism.

ticker_intc.name: Intel Corporation
ticker_intc.blurb: Intel is the world's largest semiconductor company by revenue (historically) and the only major chip company that both designs and manufactures its own processors at scale. Its product portfolio spans PC and server CPUs (Core, Xeon), AI accelerators (Gaudi), FPGAs (Altera), and networking silicon. Intel's foundry ambition — Intel Foundry Services (IFS), renamed Intel Foundry — aims to manufacture chips for external customers on its 18A and 14A process nodes, positioning the company as a Western alternative to TSMC. After CEO Pat Gelsinger was replaced in late 2024, the company has undergone significant restructuring.
ticker_intc.recent: Intel reported Q1 2026 revenue of $13.6 billion, up from a depressed base, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.29 versus a near-zero consensus — the beat sent shares up 20%+ in after-hours trading. Data-centre revenue grew 22% YoY. Full-year 2026 EPS estimates of $0.48–$0.56 would represent ~101% growth from the 2025 base — a base-effect figure that reflects restructuring charges and near-zero profitability rather than a dramatic business inflection. Intel trades at ~62.1x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.61 given the distorted growth denominator.

ticker_sndk.name: SanDisk Corporation
ticker_sndk.blurb: SanDisk was spun off from Western Digital in February 2025 as an independent pure-play NAND flash memory company. It designs and manufactures NAND-based solid-state drives, flash storage chips, and consumer memory products. The spinoff allowed the market to re-rate the business on semiconductor multiples rather than hardware-manufacturer multiples, contributing to an extraordinary post-spinoff rally driven by the NAND supercycle.
ticker_sndk.recent: Since its February 2025 spinoff, SNDK surged over 2,400% through May 2026, reaching an all-time high above $1,189. Fiscal year 2025 revenue was approximately $7.4 billion, with gross margins expanding to ~36% from the low 20s in late 2024, aided by a shift toward high-margin QLC (quad-level cell) products. Analyst targets range from $975 (Wells Fargo, Equal Weight) to $1,250 (Bernstein SocGen, Outperform). A 247 Wall St. analysis in April 2026 flagged potential overvaluation of ~32% versus peers.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

ticker_wdc.name: Western Digital Corporation
ticker_wdc.blurb: Western Digital Corporation is a leading American data storage company that designs, manufactures, and sells hard disk drives (HDDs), solid-state drives (SSDs), and flash memory solutions under brands like WD, SanDisk, and G-Technology. The company serves both consumer and enterprise markets, including cloud data centers, and is a key player in the global storage industry. Western Digital has a strong market position in HDDs and NAND flash memory, competing with Seagate and Samsung.
ticker_wdc.recent: In the past 30 days, Western Digital stock has seen positive momentum driven by strong demand for its HDD and SSD products, particularly from cloud and AI data center customers. The company reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter earnings in late October 2024, with revenue of $4.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.78, beating analyst estimates. Shares rose on the earnings beat and guidance for continued growth in the December quarter.

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

ticker_000660-ks.blurb: SK hynix Inc. researches, develops, manufactures, and sells semiconductor devices, including DRAM, NAND flash, SSD, MCP, and CMM products. The company serves server, networking, mobile, PC, consumer, and automotive markets. It is one of the world's largest memory chipmakers, competing directly with Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology.
ticker_000660-ks.recent: In the past 30 days, SK hynix reported earnings on April 23, 2026, with revenue and net income surging on a memory price upcycle. The stock hit a 52-week high of 1,653,000 KRW, reflecting strong demand for AI-related memory chips. Morningstar raised its fair value estimate by 65% following the earnings report.
